title: Think in tables: your first SQL query
objective: Read a simple table and write a SELECT query that answers a question.

segments.title: Ask a question of a table
segments.narration_text: A database table is a set of related facts. SQL lets us ask a precise question about those facts. Imagine a small table of job applications. We want to see which roles are still in progress.

payload.text: Ask a question of your data

board_events.accessible_text: The board title reads: Ask a question of your data.
A table outline appears, representing a small set of job applications.
The table has company, role, and stage columns.

payload.text: Which roles are still in progress?

board_events.accessible_text: A question appears below the table: Which roles are still in progress?
A small prepared illustration shows two rows of fictional job application data.
The stage column is highlighted as the field that can answer the question.

materials.label: Table sketch
materials.description: A sample applications table with company, role and stage columns.

checkpoint.prompt: Which column tells us whether an application is in progress?

segments.title: Read a SELECT query
segments.narration_text: SELECT names the columns we want to see. FROM names the table. WHERE keeps only rows that match a condition. Read the query from top to bottom: select company and role, from applications, where stage is interviewing.

board_events.accessible_text: The board title reads: Read a SELECT query.
A box frames a three-line SQL query.
Third line: WHERE stage equals interviewing.
An arrow connects the selected columns to the row filter.

materials.label: Query reference
materials.description: A text reference for SELECT, FROM and WHERE.

quiz.prompt: Which clause chooses the columns to show?
quiz.explanation: SELECT names the columns returned in the result.

quiz.prompt: Which clause keeps only matching rows?
quiz.explanation: WHERE applies a condition to filter rows.

descriptions: The board first shows an applications table, then a three-line SQL query.
